field-guide.json

{
  "version": "2.8.59",
  "date": "2026-09-15",
  "families": [
    {
      "id": "workbooks",
      "label": "Workbooks & sheets",
      "intent": "Give the model a home",
      "why": "The workbook holds the whole document. Worksheets divide it into named spaces; a range locates cells within one space.",
      "actions": "Create, load, rename, reorder, reset and delete.",
      "tree": "Workbook → worksheet → range",
      "settings": [
        [
          "Worksheet name",
          "string",
          "A meaningful name, used in formulas and lookup."
        ],
        [
          "Index",
          "integer",
          "Zero-based position in the sheet collection."
        ],
        [
          "Reset options",
          "object",
          "Clear cells and remove attached objects separately."
        ]
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "ranges",
      "label": "Cells & ranges",
      "intent": "Put facts and rules in the right cells",
      "why": "A range is a rectangular address. It is the main place you read or write values, formulas and formats.",
      "actions": "Read, write, fill, copy, merge and clear.",
      "tree": "Worksheet → range → cells",
      "settings": [
        [
          "target.range",
          "A1 address",
          "Which rectangle receives the write."
        ],
        [
          "values / formulas",
          "matrix",
          "Rows outside; columns inside."
        ],
        [
          "overwrite",
          "allow / error",
          "Use error to reject replacement of populated cells."
        ],
        [
          "resize",
          "auto / none",
          "Do not assume this replaces your own bounds checks."
        ]
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "formulas",
      "label": "Calculation",
      "intent": "Turn inputs into results",
      "why": "A stored formula defines a relationship. Calculation produces its value; a displayed number alone does not reveal the rule.",
      "actions": "Calculate, trace dependencies and inspect spills.",
      "tree": "Cell → formula → precedents → value",
      "settings": [
        [
          "formula",
          "string",
          "Excel-style expression beginning with =."
        ],
        [
          "References",
          "A1 or R1C1",
          "Anchor shared inputs with $ where appropriate."
        ],
        [
          "Expected result",
          "independent control",
          "Check more than the absence of error tokens."
        ]
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "formatting",
      "label": "Formatting",
      "intent": "Help the reader see structure",
      "why": "Formatting changes how cells are read: currency, hierarchy, emphasis and spacing. It usually leaves their stored values intact.",
      "actions": "Font, fill, border, alignment, units and freeze panes.",
      "tree": "Range → format → font / fill / borders",
      "settings": [
        [
          "Number format",
          "Excel format code",
          "Changes display, not numeric precision."
        ],
        [
          "Color",
          "hex / theme / object",
          "Theme colors can be reused across the workbook."
        ],
        [
          "Size",
          "points / pixels / column units",
          "Use explicit units; 30 px is 22.5 row-height points."
        ]
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "rules",
      "label": "Validation & rules",
      "intent": "Describe acceptable inputs and visible exceptions",
      "why": "Validation records input rules. Conditional formatting displays conditions. Neither is a substitute for verifying programmatic writes.",
      "actions": "Lists, bounds, custom rules, scales, bars and icons.",
      "tree": "Range → validation / conditional formats",
      "settings": [
        [
          "Type",
          "rule token",
          "List, numeric bound, custom formula, color scale and others."
        ],
        [
          "Formula / threshold",
          "value or expression",
          "The condition that the rule evaluates."
        ],
        [
          "Presentation",
          "format object",
          "What the reader sees when the condition holds."
        ]
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "tables",
      "label": "Excel Tables",
      "intent": "Turn a rectangle into a named dataset",
      "why": "An Excel Table adds headers, a name and structured references to a rectangular dataset. It is different from a pivot or a sensitivity grid.",
      "actions": "Create, append, style, set headers/totals and remove.",
      "tree": "Worksheet → table → data rows",
      "settings": [
        [
          "range",
          "A1 address",
          "Full table footprint."
        ],
        [
          "hasHeaders",
          "boolean",
          "Whether the first row contains field names."
        ],
        [
          "showTotals",
          "boolean",
          "Reserve a row: this version does not insert one."
        ],
        [
          "rows.add index",
          "null",
          "Appending works; indexed insertion is unsupported."
        ]
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "sensitivity",
      "label": "What-If tables",
      "intent": "Ask how one result changes across inputs",
      "why": "A What-If Data Table repeatedly substitutes scenario inputs into an existing calculation and records the results.",
      "actions": "One- and two-variable sensitivity grids.",
      "tree": "Formula + scenario headers → projected body",
      "settings": [
        [
          "fullRange",
          "A1 address",
          "Include the corner formula, headers and output body."
        ],
        [
          "rowInput",
          "single cell",
          "Replaced by scenario values across the top."
        ],
        [
          "columnInput",
          "single cell",
          "Replaced by scenario values down the left."
        ],
        [
          "recalculate",
          "method call",
          "Required after constructing the table."
        ]
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "pivots",
      "label": "Pivots & slicers",
      "intent": "Summarize records by category",
      "why": "A pivot aggregates source rows. A slicer filters its categories. Cached summaries and the written output area both need checks.",
      "actions": "Group fields, aggregate, filter and rebuild caches.",
      "tree": "Source → cache → pivot → slicer",
      "settings": [
        [
          "Source / destination",
          "ranges",
          "Which records are summarized, and where the result appears."
        ],
        [
          "Hierarchies",
          "field names",
          "Rows, columns and data measures."
        ],
        [
          "Creation route",
          "workbook.pivotTables",
          "The tested root route allows a slicer to find its pivot."
        ]
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "charts",
      "label": "Charts",
      "intent": "Give the numbers a visual form",
      "why": "Charts bind a visual object to data. The in-memory object, rendered picture and native Excel chart are separate outputs.",
      "actions": "Create, bind, style, annotate, position and remove.",
      "tree": "Worksheet ranges → series → chart",
      "settings": [
        [
          "Type",
          "25 enum tokens",
          "Only 16 emitted native chart XML in the tested fixtures."
        ],
        [
          "Data",
          "ranges or arrays",
          "Range references retain the link to workbook cells."
        ],
        [
          "Anchor",
          "cells / pixels",
          "Position and size on the worksheet."
        ],
        [
          "Labels / data table",
          "existing facade",
          "Mutate nested fields; plain-object replacement can break export."
        ]
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "drawings",
      "label": "Images, shapes & sparklines",
      "intent": "Add visual objects and small trends",
      "why": "Images carry pixels, shapes carry geometry and text, and sparklines display a series inside a cell. Each has its own placement and lifecycle.",
      "actions": "Add, replace, arrange, style and delete.",
      "tree": "Worksheet → drawing or sparkline group",
      "settings": [
        [
          "Source",
          "bytes / SVG / path",
          "Image insertion does not extract editable cells."
        ],
        [
          "Geometry",
          "190 tokens",
          "Custom geometry also needs path commands."
        ],
        [
          "Sparkline type",
          "line / column / stacked",
          "Three distinct small-series views."
        ],
        [
          "Anchor",
          "from + to / extent",
          "Set at creation or use the supported update operation."
        ]
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "names",
      "label": "Names",
      "intent": "Give reusable references a meaning",
      "why": "A defined name gives a range or function a stable name. Scope decides whether it belongs to the workbook or a single sheet.",
      "actions": "Named ranges and named LAMBDA functions.",
      "tree": "Workbook or worksheet → defined name",
      "settings": [
        [
          "Name / scope",
          "string / owner",
          "Avoid ambiguous worksheet and workbook definitions."
        ],
        [
          "Range",
          "qualified address",
          "The cells a name refers to."
        ],
        [
          "lambda",
          "expression",
          "The working property for named functions; not formula."
        ]
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "comments",
      "label": "Comments & notes",
      "intent": "Keep explanations beside the cells",
      "why": "Threaded comments record a conversation. A cell note records an annotation. Authors, targets and content are explicit data.",
      "actions": "Author, thread, reply, react, resolve and annotate.",
      "tree": "Author → thread / note → cell target",
      "settings": [
        [
          "Author",
          "person identity",
          "Set self before creating comments."
        ],
        [
          "Target",
          "cell or range",
          "Where the explanation belongs."
        ],
        [
          "Body",
          "text / plainText",
          "Comment and low-level note contracts differ."
        ]
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "inspection",
      "label": "Inspection & discovery",
      "intent": "Understand before changing",
      "why": "Help describes available calls. Inspect describes an actual workbook. Resolve turns an inspected identity into an editable object.",
      "actions": "Help, inspect, search, resolve and trace.",
      "tree": "Question → bounded evidence → editable object",
      "settings": [
        [
          "kind",
          "record types",
          "Sheets, formulas, tables, charts, threads and names."
        ],
        [
          "target",
          "observed anchor ID",
          "Use real IDs returned by inspection."
        ],
        [
          "maxChars",
          "integer",
          "Bound the response; check truncation."
        ]
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "files",
      "label": "Files & rendering",
      "intent": "Move between representations",
      "why": "Import creates an editable workbook. Rendering creates pixels. Export creates a saved file. Re-import tests a different boundary again.",
      "actions": "CSV, Markdown, HTML, XLSX, PNG, JPEG and layout evidence.",
      "tree": "Source file → workbook → pixels / native file",
      "settings": [
        [
          "Format",
          "png / jpeg / layout / xlsx",
          "These are the tested workbook export formats."
        ],
        [
          "View",
          "sheet / range / crop",
          "Choose the relevant portion to render."
        ],
        [
          "Return type",
          "Blob or saved descriptor",
          "Managed sessions write files and return descriptors."
        ]
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "changes",
      "label": "Changes & sessions",
      "intent": "Wrap edits in a repeatable process",
      "why": "Direct edits change an object. Recorded patches describe changes. Shared updates carry collaborative history. Sessions persist work across calls.",
      "actions": "Record, apply, undo, replicate and resume.",
      "tree": "Code → edit → patch / update → saved session",
      "settings": [
        [
          "Warnings",
          "returned array",
          "Unknown operations can warn while earlier changes remain."
        ],
        [
          "Baseline",
          "shared CRDT history",
          "Identical JSON is not identical collaborative history."
        ],
        [
          "Session target",
          "file, snapshot or ID",
          "Reopen the same target across calls."
        ],
        [
          "Timeout",
          "1–300,000 ms",
          "Inspect saved state after an ambiguous timeout."
        ]
      ]
    }
  ],

        "stderr": ""
      },
      "code": "import fs from \"node:fs/promises\";\n\nimport { SpreadsheetFile, Workbook } from \"@oai/artifact-tool\";\n\n/**\n * Quick Start Examples\n * This runnable TypeScript example mirrors:\n * lib/agent/tools/artifact_tool_v2/skills/python/spreadsheets/examples/quick_start_example.py\n */\nasync function quickApiExample(): Promise<void> {\n  // Creating a workbook and adding sheets with data and basic formatting\n  const workbook = Workbook.create();\n  var sheet = workbook.worksheets.add(\"ExampleSheet\");\n\n  sheet = workbook.worksheets.getItem(\"ExampleSheet\");\n  sheet.getRange(\"A1:D4\").values = [\n    [\"Name\", \"Personality Type\", \"Age\", \"Birthday\"],\n    [\"John Doe\", \"Introvert\", 30, new Date(\"1990-01-01T00:00:00Z\")],\n    [\"Jane Smith\", \"Extrovert\", 25, new Date(\"1995-02-15T00:00:00Z\")],\n    [\"Jim Very Long Name\", \"Ambivert\", 40, new Date(\"1980-03-20T00:00:00Z\")],\n  ];\n  sheet.getRange(\"E1\").values = [[\"Score\"]];\n  sheet.getRange(\"E2\").formulas = [[\"=C2*10\"]]; // score is 10 * age\n  sheet.getRange(\"E2:E4\").fillDown();\n  const headerRange = sheet.getRange(\"A1:E1\");\n\n  // Styling\n  const headerFormats = {\n    fill: \"#0F766E\",\n    font: { bold: true, color: \"#FFFFFF\" },\n    horizontalAlignment: \"center\",\n    verticalAlignment: \"center\",\n    rowHeight: 16,\n  };\n  headerRange.format = headerFormats;\n  headerRange.format.autofitColumns();\n\n  const dataRange = sheet.getRange(\"A2:D4\");\n  dataRange.format.wrapText = true;\n  sheet.showGridLines = false;\n\n  // Format dates properly.\n  sheet.getRange(\"D2:D4\").format.numberFormat = \"MM/DD/YYYY\";\n\n  // Conditional formatting\n  sheet.getRange(\"C2:C4\").conditionalFormats.add(\"dataBar\", {\n    color: \"#704023\",\n    gradient: true,\n  });\n  sheet.getRange(\"E2:E4\").conditionalFormats.add(\"cellIs\", {\n    operator: \"greaterThan\",\n    formula: 300,\n    format: { font: { color: \"#B91C1C\" } },\n  });\n  sheet.conditionalFormattings.add({\n    range: \"B2:B4\",\n    rule: {\n      type: \"expression\",\n      formula: '=B2=\"Introvert\"',\n      format: { fill: \"#FCA5A5\" },\n    },\n  });\n\n  // Data validation: Since Personality Type is a dropdown category, add data validation.\n  sheet.getRange(\"B2:B4\").dataValidation = {\n    rule: {\n      type: \"list\",\n      values: [\"Introvert\", \"Extrovert\", \"Ambivert\"],\n      // formula1: \"CategoriesSheet!$A$2:$A$4\", // Alternative: reference a tunable list\n    },\n  };\n\n  // Tables: Turn it into a table (for example purposes! Make sure table names are unique)\n  // NOTE: If hasHeaders=true, the range must include the header row.\n  const table = sheet.tables.add(\"A1:E4\", true, \"PeopleTable\");\n  table.getHeaderRowRange();\n\n  // First column is still wide since we only auto-fit the first row. Expand it manually.\n  sheet.getRange(\"A1:A4\").format.columnWidth = 20;\n\n  // Create a compact chart helper range that references the source table.\n  sheet.getRange(\"H1:I1\").merge();\n  sheet.getRange(\"H1\").values = [[\"Charts\"]];\n  sheet.getRange(\"H1\").format = headerFormats;\n  sheet.getRange(\"H3:I3\").values = [[\"Person\", \"Score\"]];\n  sheet.getRange(\"H4:I4\").formulas = [[\"=A2\", \"=E2\"]];\n  sheet.getRange(\"H4:I6\").fillDown();\n  const chart = sheet.charts.add(\"bar\", sheet.getRange(\"H3:I6\"));\n  chart.title = \"Person by Scores\";\n  chart.hasLegend = true;\n  chart.displayBlanksAs = \"zero\";\n  chart.barOptions.direction = \"column\";\n  chart.barOptions.grouping = \"clustered\";\n  chart.setPosition(\"K2\", \"R16\");\n\n  // Granular control over chart axes\n  chart.xAxis = {\n    axisType: \"textAxis\",\n    title: { text: \"Person\", textStyle: { fontSize: 13, bold: true } },\n    position: \"bottom\",\n    orientation: \"minMax\",\n    textStyle: { fontSize: 10 },\n  };\n  chart.yAxis = {\n    axisType: \"textAxis\",\n    title: { text: \"Scores\", textStyle: { fontSize: 13, bold: true } },\n    numberFormatCode: \"0,000\",\n    numberFormatSourceLinked: false,\n  };\n\n  // Sparklines: add to the right of table\n  const sparklinesHeader = sheet.getRange(\"F1\");\n  sparklinesHeader.values = [[\"Sparklines\"]];\n  sparklinesHeader.format = headerFormats;\n  sparklinesHeader.format.autofitColumns();\n\n  sheet.sparklines.add({\n    type: \"column\", // \"line\" | \"column\" | \"stacked\"\n    sourceData: sheet.getRange(\"E2:E4\"),\n    targetRange: sheet.getRange(\"F2:F4\"),\n    seriesColor: \"#AAAAAA\",\n  });\n\n  // Render\n  await fs.mkdir(\"output\", { recursive: true });\n  const pngBlob = await workbook.render({\n    sheetName: \"ExampleSheet\",\n    autoCrop: \"all\",\n    scale: 1,\n    format: \"png\",\n  });\n  const pngBytes = new Uint8Array(await pngBlob.arrayBuffer());\n  await fs.writeFile(\"output/example_sheet.png\", pngBytes);\n  console.log(\"Rendered first sheet to 'output/example_sheet.png'\");\n\n  // Export\n  const out = \"output/example_sheet.xlsx\";\n  const xlsx = await SpreadsheetFile.exportXlsx(workbook);\n  await xlsx.save(out);\n  console.log(`Spreadsheet saved to ${out}`);\n}\n\nquickApiExample().catch((error: unknown) => {\n  console.error(error);\n  process.exit(1);\n});\n",

      "code": "import { Workbook } from \"@oai/artifact-tool\";\n\nfunction clip(value: string, maxChars: number): string {\n  return value.length > maxChars ? `${value.slice(0, maxChars)}...` : value;\n}\n\nfunction summarizeTrace(\n  root: any,\n  options: { maxDepth?: number; maxNodes?: number; maxFormulaChars?: number } = {},\n): string[] {\n  if (!root) return [\"(no trace returned)\"];\n\n  const maxDepth = options.maxDepth ?? 4;\n  const maxNodes = options.maxNodes ?? 30;\n  const maxFormulaChars = options.maxFormulaChars ?? 120;\n  const lines: string[] = [];\n  let nodeCount = 0;\n  let truncated = false;\n\n  function walk(node: any, depth: number): void {\n    if (nodeCount >= maxNodes) {\n      truncated = true;\n      return;\n    }\n\n    nodeCount += 1;\n    const indent = \"  \".repeat(depth);\n    const formula = node.formula\n      ? ` formula=${clip(String(node.formula), maxFormulaChars)}`\n      : \"\";\n    const error = node.error ? ` error=${node.error}` : \"\";\n    lines.push(`${indent}${node.cell} value=${JSON.stringify(node.value)}${formula}${error}`);\n\n    const children = (node.params ?? []) as any[];\n    if (children.length === 0) return;\n    if (depth >= maxDepth) {\n      truncated = true;\n      lines.push(`${indent}  ... ${children.length} precedent(s) not shown`);\n      return;\n    }\n    for (const child of children) {\n      walk(child, depth + 1);\n    }\n  }\n\n  walk(root, 0);\n  if (truncated) lines.push(`... trace summary capped at depth ${maxDepth}, ${maxNodes} nodes`);\n  return lines;\n}\n\nfunction findTraceNode(root: any, cell: string): any | null {\n  if (!root) return null;\n  if (root.cell === cell) return root;\n  for (const child of (root.params ?? []) as any[]) {\n    const found = findTraceNode(child, cell);\n    if (found) return found;\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\nfunction formatNumber(value: unknown): string {\n  if (typeof value !== \"number\") return String(value);\n  if (value !== 0 && Math.abs(value) < 0.01) return Number(value.toPrecision(3)).toString();\n  return value.toLocaleString(\"en-US\", { maximumFractionDigits: 2 });\n}\n\nfunction formatPercent(value: unknown): string {\n  return typeof value === \"number\" ? `${(value * 100).toFixed(1)}%` : String(value);\n}\n\nfunction explainRevenueCheck(trace: any): string {\n  const status = findTraceNode(trace, \"Checks!F2\")?.value;\n  const difference = findTraceNode(trace, \"Checks!D2\")?.value;\n  const actual = findTraceNode(trace, \"Checks!B2\")?.value;\n  const expected = findTraceNode(trace, \"Checks!C2\")?.value;\n  const tolerance = findTraceNode(trace, \"Checks!E2\")?.value;\n  const baseRevenue = findTraceNode(trace, \"Inputs!B2\")?.value;\n  const growthRate = findTraceNode(trace, \"Inputs!B3\")?.value;\n  const revenue2025 = findTraceNode(trace, \"Model!B4\")?.value;\n\n  return [\n    `Checks!F2 returns \"${status}\" because the absolute difference is within the tolerance.`,\n    `It compares Checks!D2 (${formatNumber(difference)}) against Checks!E2 (${formatNumber(tolerance)}).`,\n    `Checks!D2 is actual revenue minus expected revenue: Checks!B2 (${formatNumber(actual)}) - Checks!C2 (${formatNumber(expected)}).`,\n    `The actual value comes from Model!B5, which compounds Inputs!B2 (${formatNumber(baseRevenue)}) by the growth rate in Inputs!B3 (${formatPercent(growthRate)}) for two years: first to Model!B4 (${formatNumber(revenue2025)}), then to Model!B5 (${formatNumber(actual)}).`,\n    `Caveat: the tiny difference shown is floating-point rounding noise, not a business variance.`,\n  ].join(\"\\n\");\n}\n\nasync function main(): Promise<void> {\n  const workbook = Workbook.create();\n  const inputs = workbook.worksheets.add(\"Inputs\");\n  const model = workbook.worksheets.add(\"Model\");\n  const checks = workbook.worksheets.add(\"Checks\");\n\n  inputs.getRange(\"A1:B4\").values = [\n    [\"Metric\", \"Value\"],\n    [\"Revenue 2024\", 100],\n    [\"Growth Rate\", 0.1],\n    [\"Expected Revenue 2026\", 121],\n  ];\n\n  model.getRange(\"A1:B5\").values = [\n    [\"Metric\", \"Value\"],\n    [\"Revenue 2024\", null],\n    [\"Growth Rate\", null],\n    [\"Revenue 2025\", null],\n    [\"Revenue 2026\", null],\n  ];\n  model.getRange(\"B2:B5\").formulas = [\n    [\"=Inputs!B2\"],\n    [\"=Inputs!B3\"],\n    [\"=B2*(1+B3)\"],\n    [\"=B4*(1+B3)\"],\n  ];\n\n  checks.getRange(\"A1:F2\").values = [\n    [\"Check\", \"Actual\", \"Expected\", \"Difference\", \"Tolerance\", \"Status\"],\n    [\"Revenue 2026 ties to expected case\", null, null, null, 0.001, null],\n  ];\n  checks.getRange(\"B2:D2\").formulas = [[\"=Model!B5\", \"=Inputs!B4\", \"=B2-C2\"]];\n  checks.getRange(\"F2\").formulas = [[\"=IF(ABS(D2)<=E2,\\\"OK\\\",\\\"CHECK\\\")\"]];\n\n  workbook.recalculate();\n  const trace = workbook.trace(\"Checks!F2\");\n\n  console.log(\"=== Formula trace for Checks!F2 ===\");\n  console.log(\n    summarizeTrace(trace, {\n      maxDepth: 4,\n      maxNodes: 20,\n    }).join(\"\\n\"),\n  );\n\n  console.log(\"\\n=== User-facing answer: How is Checks!F2 calculated? ===\");\n  console.log(explainRevenueCheck(trace));\n\n  console.log(\"\\n=== Exact formula help: XLOOKUP ===\");\n  console.log(\n    workbook.help(\"fx.XLOOKUP\", {\n      include: \"index,examples,notes\",\n      maxChars: 2500,\n    }).ndjson,\n  );\n\n  console.log(\"\\n=== Formula category browse: financial ===\");\n  console.log(\n    workbook.help(\"fx.*\", {\n      search: \"financial\",\n      include: \"index,examples\",\n      maxChars: 2500,\n    }).ndjson,\n  );\n\n  console.log(\"\\n=== Formula category browse: math-trig ===\");\n  console.log(\n    workbook.help(\"fx.*\", {\n      search: \"math-trig\",\n      include: \"index,examples\",\n      maxChars: 2500,\n    }).ndjson,\n  );\n\n  console.log(\"\\n=== Semantic formula search: lookup with fallback ===\");\n  console.log(\n    workbook.help(\"lookup value with fallback\", {\n      search: \"XLOOKUP|INDEX|MATCH|IFERROR\",\n      include: \"index,examples,notes\",\n      maxChars: 3000,\n    }).ndjson,\n  );\n}\n\nmain().catch((error: unknown) => {\n  console.error(error);\n  process.exit(1);\n});\n",

      "code": "import fs from \"node:fs/promises\";\n\nimport { SpreadsheetFile, Workbook, ChartDataLabels } from \"@oai/artifact-tool\";\n\nasync function buildChartSuggestionWorkbook(outputDir: string): Promise<void> {\n  await fs.mkdir(outputDir, { recursive: true });\n\n  const workbook = Workbook.create();\n  const sheet = workbook.worksheets.add(\"Charts\");\n  sheet.showGridLines = false;\n\n  sheet.getRange(\"A1:C5\").values = [\n    [\"Month\", \"Revenue\", \"EBITDA\"],\n    [\"Jan\", 100000, 18000],\n    [\"Feb\", 121000, 23000],\n    [\"Mar\", 132000, 28000],\n    [\"Apr\", 149000, 34000],\n  ];\n  sheet.getRange(\"A1:C1\").format = {\n    fill: \"#0F766E\",\n    font: { bold: true, color: \"#FFFFFF\" },\n  };\n  sheet.getRange(\"B2:C5\").format.numberFormat = \"$#,##0\";\n  sheet.getRange(\"A:C\").format.columnWidthPx = 96;\n\n  // Fast chart path: chart a continuous helper range. The helper range is\n  // formula-backed so edits to the source table update the chart.\n  sheet.getRange(\"F1:H1\").values = [[\"Month\", \"Revenue\", \"EBITDA\"]];\n  sheet.getRange(\"F2:H2\").formulas = [[\"=A2\", \"=B2\", \"=C2\"]];\n  sheet.getRange(\"F2:H5\").fillDown();\n  const lineChart = sheet.charts.add(\"line\", sheet.getRange(\"F1:H5\"));\n  lineChart.setPosition(\"J1\", \"Q15\");\n  lineChart.title = \"Revenue and EBITDA Trend\";\n  lineChart.titleTextStyle.fontSize = 12;\n  lineChart.hasLegend = true;\n  lineChart.xAxis = { axisType: \"textAxis\" };\n  lineChart.yAxis = { numberFormatCode: \"$#,##0\" };\n\n  const scatterPlot = sheet.charts.add(\"scatter\", sheet.getRange(\"F1:H5\"));\n  scatterPlot.setPosition(\"J1\", \"Q15\");\n  scatterPlot.title = \"Revenue and EBITDA Trend Scatter\";\n  scatterPlot.titleTextStyle.fontSize = 12;\n  scatterPlot.hasLegend = true;\n  scatterPlot.xAxis = { axisType: \"textAxis\" };\n  scatterPlot.yAxis = { numberFormatCode: \"$#,##0\" };\n  scatterPlot.dataLabels = new ChartDataLabels({showValue: true, position: 'above' });\n\n  // Advanced path: manually define a single series by formula.\n  const barChart = sheet.charts.add(\"bar\", {\n    title: \"EBITDA by Month\",\n    hasLegend: false,\n  });\n  const series = barChart.series.add(\"EBITDA\");\n  series.categoryFormula = \"'Charts'!$A$2:$A$5\";\n  series.formula = \"'Charts'!$C$2:$C$5\";\n  series.fill = \"#F472B6\";\n  barChart.setPosition(\"J18\", \"Q32\");\n  barChart.title = \"EBITDA by Month\";\n  barChart.titleTextStyle.fontSize = 12;\n  barChart.xAxis = { axisType: \"textAxis\", textStyle: { fontSize: 10} };\n  barChart.yAxis = { numberFormatCode: \"$#,##0\", textStyle: { fontSize: 10} };\n\n  barChart.xAxis.title.text = \"EBITDA\";  \n\n  barChart.yAxis.title.text = \"Month\";\n  barChart.yAxis.min = 10_000;\n  barChart.yAxis.max = 40_000;\n  barChart.yAxis.majorUnit = 5;\n  // TODO @vicky set default title text to be size 12\n\n  // setData replaces the chart source range; use it when a chart exists before\n  // the final source range is known.\n  lineChart.setData(sheet.getRange(\"F1:H5\"));\n\n  const preview = await workbook.render({\n    sheetName: \"Charts\",\n    autoCrop: \"all\",\n    scale: 1,\n    format: \"png\",\n  });\n  await fs.writeFile(\n    `${outputDir}/typescript_chart_suggestions.png`,\n    new Uint8Array(await preview.arrayBuffer()),\n  );\n\n  const xlsx = await SpreadsheetFile.exportXlsx(workbook);\n  await xlsx.save(`${outputDir}/typescript_chart_suggestions.xlsx`);\n\n  console.log(`Rendered ${outputDir}/typescript_chart_suggestions.png`);\n  console.log(`Saved ${outputDir}/typescript_chart_suggestions.xlsx`);\n}\n\nconst outputDir = process.argv[2] ?? \"output/chart_suggestions\";\nbuildChartSuggestionWorkbook(outputDir).catch((error: unknown) => {\n  console.error(error);\n  process.exit(1);\n});\n",

      "code": "import * as fs from \"node:fs/promises\";\nimport * as path from \"node:path\";\n\nimport {\n  FileBlob,\n  SpreadsheetFile,\n} from \"../../../../oai_js_artifact_tool\";\n\nconst DEFAULT_WORKBOOK_INPUTS = [\n  \"/Users/vicky/code/openai/output/spreadsheet-atv/fitness-tracker-20260409\",\n];\n\ntype InspectResult = {\n  ndjson: string;\n};\n\nasync function resolveWorkbookPath(inputPath: string): Promise<string> {\n  const expandedPath = inputPath.startsWith(\"~\")\n    ? path.join(process.env.HOME ?? \"\", inputPath.slice(1))\n    : inputPath;\n  const stats = await fs.stat(expandedPath);\n  if (stats.isFile()) {\n    return expandedPath;\n  }\n  if (stats.isDirectory()) {\n    const candidates = (await fs.readdir(expandedPath))\n      .filter((entry) => entry.endsWith(\".xlsx\"))\n      .sort();\n    if (candidates.length > 0) {\n      return path.join(expandedPath, candidates[0]);\n    }\n    throw new Error(`No .xlsx files found in directory: ${expandedPath}`);\n  }\n  throw new Error(`Workbook path is not a file or directory: ${expandedPath}`);\n}\n\nfunction printInspect(title: string, result: InspectResult): void {\n  console.log(`\\n=== ${title} ===`);\n  if (result.ndjson) {\n    console.log(result.ndjson);\n    return;\n  }\n  console.log(\"(no rows returned)\");\n}\n\nasync function inspectWorkbook(workbookPath: string): Promise<void> {\n  const workbook = await SpreadsheetFile.importXlsx(await FileBlob.load(workbookPath));\n  const firstSheet = workbook.worksheets.getItemAt(0);\n  const firstSheetName = firstSheet.name;\n\n  console.log(`\\n########## Inspecting ${workbookPath} ##########`);\n  console.log(`First worksheet: ${firstSheetName}`);\n\n  const summary = await workbook.inspect({\n    kind: \"workbook,sheet,table\",\n    maxChars: 6000,\n    tableMaxRows: 6,\n    tableMaxCols: 6,\n    tableMaxCellChars: 80,\n  });\n  printInspect(\"Workbook summary\", summary);\n\n  const sheetsIndex = await workbook.inspect({\n    kind: \"sheet\",\n    include: \"id,name\",\n  });\n  printInspect(\"Sheets index\", sheetsIndex);\n\n  const firstRegion = await workbook.inspect({\n    kind: \"region\",\n    sheetId: firstSheetName,\n    range: \"A1:Z30\",\n    maxChars: 2500,\n    tableMaxRows: 12,\n    tableMaxCols: 8,\n    tableMaxCellChars: 50,\n  });\n  printInspect(`First sheet region preview (${firstSheetName}!A1:Z30)`, firstRegion);\n\n  const formulas = await workbook.inspect({\n    kind: \"formula\",\n    sheetId: firstSheetName,\n    maxChars: 2000,\n  });\n  printInspect(`Formula snapshot (${firstSheetName})`, formulas);\n\n  const drawings = await workbook.inspect({\n    kind: \"drawing\",\n    sheetId: firstSheetName,\n    maxChars: 2000,\n  });\n  printInspect(`Drawing snapshot (${firstSheetName})`, drawings);\n}\n\nasync function inspectExistingWorkbooks(inputPaths: string[]): Promise<void> {\n  for (const inputPath of inputPaths) {\n    const workbookPath = await resolveWorkbookPath(inputPath);\n    await inspectWorkbook(workbookPath);\n  }\n}\n\nasync function main(): Promise<void> {\n  const inputPaths =\n    process.argv.slice(2).length > 0\n      ? process.argv.slice(2)\n      : DEFAULT_WORKBOOK_INPUTS;\n  await inspectExistingWorkbooks(inputPaths);\n}\n\nmain().catch((error: unknown) => {\n  console.error(error);\n  process.exit(1);\n});\n",

      "code": "# Workflows for creating new spreadsheets\n\n## Quality Guidelines\n- Build correct, readable, auditable workbooks for the intended audience; keep them simple and easy to update.\n- Before populating, identify the audience, decision, target engine, outputs, inputs, calculations and checks from the user request, reference/template and applicable domain guidance. These roles do not require tabs: combine compatible roles and add tabs only for distinct readers, dependencies, refresh boundaries, auditability or an explicit request.\n- Keep related inputs and calculation steps together. Calculate each result in one place and link to it from other views. Do not create a tab for a small supporting block that fits cleanly in an existing sheet.\n- Put requested insights or recommendations once on the main dashboard, cover or summary. If none exists, place them near the relevant results. Support them with figures or rules already shown. Avoid generic rationale, invented scoring or long formula-generated narrative. Keep useful short calculated statuses and actions.\n- For triage, priorities or next actions, make records needing attention and the reasons easy to find, using formatting for visual cues to highlight important items needing attention. Include owners, actions or deadlines when relevant and supported by the data. Keep summary counts traceable to those records.\n- Reduce oversized widths/heights after autofit without clipping content.\n\n## Checks\n- Do not add a separate \"Checks\" tab for simple spreadsheets. Only add when useful for task/complexity.\n",

      },
      "code": "# Editing an existing spreadsheet\n\nTreat existing workbook as the reference: preserve its structure, formula patterns, formatting, terminology, and navigation and extend nearby conventions unless the user explicitly requests a change.\n\nUser requests always take priority over any rules in this file.\n\n## Safety rules\n- Do not add, remove, rename, reorder, or split tabs unless requested or required.\n- Before modifying: ALWAYS study and match the existing format, style and conventions when making edits by rendering and viewing the image. Read related values and formulas.\n\n## Important guidelines\n- Prioritize consistency unless it conflicts with user request: Ensure existing formulas, layouts, structures, and patterns are consistent. For example, if asked to add another column or row to a table and there is conditional formatting applied to the whole table, it should extend to the new column or rows as well.\n- Keep edits targeted unless a broader change is clearly necessary. Exceptions are when there's dependencies, e.g. a dynamic chart that is based on the range of values in a table and a new row is added, the chart should also update.\n- Change only requested cells and directly affected formulas/charts. Preserve unrelated tabs, formulas, formatting, validations, named ranges, comments, protection, hidden/grouped rows/columns, freeze panes and chart content. Do not add sheets, rows, columns or helpers unless requested.\n- Never overwrite formatting for spreadsheets with established formats, unless requested or to extend an added range.\n- Preserve native tables, structured references, pivot sources, shared formulas, filters, external links, INDIRECT routing and calculation/iteration settings. Do not flatten formulas or rebuild unrelated features for convenience.\n- For visual fixes, start with the smallest plausible local change. Do not apply sheet-wide autofit, wrapping, or restyling unless requested.\n\n## Formula Rules\n\nFor formula edits, follow the user's request first; otherwise preserve valid existing conventions before applying defaults for new formulas.\n\n- Preserve valid existing formula conventions, structure and references to editable inputs unless the user requests otherwise. Look at a couple examples in the requested edit area before making changes.\n- If there are any errors with the original workbook, unrelated to the task at hand, do not fix them arbitrarily. Instead, summarize the issues to the user and ask if they want them fixed.\n",
      "source": "../2026-09-15-artifact-tool-reference/files/sources/skill/workflows/edit_workflows.md",
      "notes": [
        "The concise working pattern is a reading aid. The complete archived document is available under Code and saved record.",

      "code": "# Style and Formatting Instructions\n\nFollow user instructions, then intentional templates/references, then domain guidance. Defaults apply only to new sheets or authorized restyling.\n\nRender before editing. Preserve unrelated content, layout, formatting and native features; values-only edits must not change formatting.\n\n## Tab Structure Defaults\n- Follow [Workbook Structure](SKILL.md#workbook-structure) and [Build Structure and Formula Flow](SKILL.md#build-structure-and-formula-flow). Roles do not require separate tabs: keep simple workbooks basic and apply role styling by section on mixed-use tabs.\n- Keep primary outputs and the assumptions control panel easy to find. Use a dark brand-color tab for outputs and one level lighter for Assumptions; standalone Finance Actuals tabs use light tan. Preserve intentional user/reference colors.\n- For complex workbooks with several source/internal tabs after the working views, place a divider before that group. Do not add dividers for focused tasks. Choose a plain name that fits the group, such as `Data >>`, `Internal >>` or `Inputs >>`. Color the divider and leave its children uncolored, overriding individual role colors. Give any `ReadMe` tab a distinct muted color, including within a divider group. Leave other tabs uncolored unless color clarifies navigation.\n\n## Reader-facing sheet layout\n\nFor new reader-facing sheets or authorized restyling, use a compact, presentation-style opening view: a concise unfilled title, modest whitespace and the main results. Choose a table, chart or both to suit the task. Covers follow the simple front-page guidance in Workbook Structure instead of the layout below.\n\nFor a filled Cover, start with a bounded area such as `A1:Z100` and adjust it to the intended opening view. Never apply the background to the entire worksheet or whole rows/columns.\n\n- Use one blank top row, then a concise unfilled left-aligned title, a thin rule and compact spacing before the main content. Include essential context, not a required subtitle or takeaway. Avoid large filled title banners. This presentation default does not add blank rows to raw source tables or override a supplied layout.\n- Remove filler. Put useful table commentary in ordinary `Notes` or `Comments` cells to the right, separated by at least one blank spacer column and outside the table header fill and borders. Turn wrapping off. Widen or shorten notes without increasing the table row heights; put longer required explanations in a separate notes area on the same sheet. Keep notes readable and unclipped. Do not add setup/footer blocks. Keep essential units and specific warnings beside the affected result. Follow [Citation Requirements](SKILL.md#citation-requirements) for sources and annotations. These are ordinary cells, not Excel Comments or Notes.\n- Add summary/KPI cards only when they clarify the requested decision; do not duplicate a small table or make oversized cards.\n- Choose cards, tables and charts for the task; keep useful trends and comparisons rather than defaulting every summary to a table. Use the width of an analytical Summary: place a compact table beside a useful chart and monthly detail below when that fits the content. Do not turn it into a tall page of prose or shrink fonts to force a layout.\n\n## Use a visually clear layout\n- Distinguish headers, inputs, calculations and notes consistently. Default to dark body text and restrained fills, not a universal teal theme. Preserve domain styling defaults, like finance input/formula/source colors and dynamic statuses.\n- When cases are used, including outside Finance, show `Case Selected:` and the linked case value (for example, `Base`) prominently near the top of each output and build tab. Center the value horizontally and vertically in a restrained dashed or dotted outline, close to the content. Keep one editable selector and distinguish the active case from actuals and named comparison cases. On Assumptions, put the selector or its linked value and only essential global inputs directly above the driver table. Emphasize each driver's Active Selection row over its case inputs. Include a short case-number key only for numeric selectors. Do not add unused Owner columns or setup sections, and preserve meaningful existing owners.\n- Put purely technical helper rows, such as period keys, above the model; italicize and group/collapse them where supported. Keep them inspectable but out of business headers and chart labels. Do not hide useful business calculation steps as helpers.\n- On output tabs, use consistent row heights within each table and modest vertical padding. Tighten excessive spacing and reduce oversized heights after autofit while keeping useful breathing room and readability when tables are copied into slides or printed to PDF. Size rows to the font and content; expand only rows needing wrapped table content, not the whole table, and do not shrink fonts to tighten spacing. Exclude off-table commentary from table-row autofit. Input tabs can use smaller, fitted rows; keep working builds compact. Apply these distinctions by section on mixed-use tabs. Format only populated or intentionally reserved ranges.\n- Keep working titles, headers and input/calculation areas unmerged. Presentation merges require user/template intent; never overwrite content or combine distinct table columns. In reader-facing tables, center column headers horizontally and vertically. For one heading spanning several otherwise empty header cells, use Center Across Selection where supported, or simplify the layout to one header cell. Treat the span as one header group with no internal borders or blank outlined header boxes; never center across distinct headings or populated cells. Working builds may retain useful blank column headers and genuine spacer columns.\n- Use yellow/amber for inputs needing updates. Distinguish editable-input cues from calculated warnings, with a compact legend when needed. Follow documented exception styles for overrides, special formulas and one-offs.\n- Dark column headers: white text with thin white separators between actual headings, including dates.\n- Section bands: continuous fill and one outside outline, without internal borders; exclude gutters. Keep genuine spacer columns between separate tables or sections blank and unfilled, including their header cells.\n- If a sheet uses a leading gutter, align titles, sections and tables to the same content edge. Keep it empty except for specified navigation markers. Follow Finance gutter defaults only for financial models; do not impose them on operational trackers.\n- Prefer thin/light structural borders, stronger section breaks and no full body-cell grid. Do not apply borders around every filled cell. \n- Hide worksheet gridlines by default on new sheets, including inputs, builds and outputs. Preserve an intentional user/reference setting and do not change gridlines during unrelated edits. Gridline visibility is separate from selective structural borders.\n- Put needed context in separate cells or ordinary punctuation. Preserve meaningful financial/mathematical labels and symbols, required source quotes, intentional reference conventions and the expressly specified plain `x` navigation markers.\n- Use bounded conditional formatting for status, risk, variance and exception cues that must react to edits. Reuse the workbook's existing rules rather than inventing business logic for color. Emphasize affected missing/invalid inputs or failed checks, for example with light-red fill and bold red text for critical errors. Keep valid check values neutral. Do not substitute static error paint or decorative PASS fills.\n\n## Freeze panes\n\n- For tables that need vertical scrolling, freeze the header rows. Freeze identifying columns when horizontal scrolling would hide them. Use the smallest useful frozen area. Leave enough space to read and work with the data.\n- Do not move content or add tabs to accommodate freezing. Preserve existing panes during unrelated edits.\n- Do not freeze compact summary, dashboard or cover sheets unless scrolling requires preserving shared headers or row labels.\n\n## Align and format by data type\n\n- Left-align text, right-align numbers and center column headers horizontally. Default to middle vertical alignment throughout populated and intentionally reserved workbook ranges. Top-align wrapped descriptions where helpful.\n- Keep numbers/dates typed with explicit, appropriate formats and clear units. Adjust widths/heights so final content with formatting fits (including signs, parenthesis and units); never stringify values for appearance.\n- Italicize brief context/scope/unit notes—not headers, controls, statuses or warnings.\n\n## Typography - Use intentionally but conservatively\n\n- Choose one font verified in both generating and target environments: Helvetica Neue → Helvetica → Arial → Aptos. Use one family across cells, charts and theme fonts, with consistent body sizing across the workbook. \n- Default to two font sizes, max three, across standard non-cover sheets, keeping sizes consistent for matching elements. Dashboard and visual sheets may use additional sizes selectively but keep them modest.\n- Keep the largest size no more than 6 pt above the body size, unless the user or reference specifies otherwise. Use spacing and restrained fills for hierarchy.\n- Example defaults: 10pt body/table headers, 14pt for titles, 16pt ceiling.\n- Table headers and content should typically be consistent following the chosen body size.\n- Use bold or italics sparingly for emphasis. For example for totals or when needed for domain styling defaults.\n\n## Live inputs and visuals\n\n- Drive dependent values, charts and status text from editable cells. Use categorical validation where feasible and the dynamic-state formatting above. Invalid/missing inputs must not appear as plausible zeros or success states.\n- Prefer compact, formula-linked summaries. Preserve required outputs; avoid redundant tables and oversized KPI cards. Inline bars require explicit request. Follow `features/charts.md` for charts.\n",
      "source": "../2026-09-15-artifact-tool-reference/files/sources/skill/style_guidelines.md",
      "notes": [
        "The concise working pattern is a reading aid. The complete archived document is available under Code and saved record.",

      "title": "Structure a financial model",
      "kind": "guidance",
      "category": "Supplied workflow guidance",
      "status": "Guidance only",
      "summary": "Connect periods, assumptions and schedules to useful outputs and reconciliations.",
      "input": {
        "whenToUse": "Connect periods, assumptions and schedules to useful outputs and reconciliations.",
        "scope": "Guidance around the package; not an additional API"
      },
      "result": {
        "workingPattern": [
          "Keep periods and accounting bases consistent.",
          "Calculate meaningful intermediate results once.",
          "Use independent checks for terminal answers."
        ],
        "source": "files/sources/skill/domain_guidance/financial_models.md"
      },
      "code": "# Finance Guidance\n\nUse for financial planning, reporting, operating models and valuation. The main skill governs structure, formulas and verification; [shared style](../style_guidelines.md) governs general formatting.\n\n## Financial Basis and Sources\n\nPreserve reference drivers and schedules. Keep scope, accounting basis, inclusions/exclusions, periods, currency, scale and signs consistent. Distinguish revenue from collections, payroll expense from cash paid, capex from depreciation, and earnings from cash flow. Explain material differences and estimates; do not imply FX conversion or round stored values for display.\n\nFollow [Citation Requirements](../SKILL.md#citation-requirements). Reconcile source controls before combining extracts or comparing versions. Use concise period/unit labels; do not add a redundant Units column.\n\n## Periods, Assumptions and Scenarios\n\nUse the source fiscal calendar, cutoff, horizon and grain. Use source actual/forecast labels. Use editable dated drivers even when flat. Keep inputs and commentary tied to absolute dates as horizons advance.\n\nWith monthly pay and no proration, $60,000 actual salary / 10 paid FTE implies $6,000/FTE. Forecast Base/Downside pay of $6,300/$6,000 with 11 paid FTE gives $69,300/$66,000; actual salary stays $60,000. Missing pay or zero FTE cannot establish an implied rate.\n\nFor refreshes, merge complete periods on business/date keys, preserving history and excluding overlaps. Do not roll headers over stationary inputs. Distinguish one-time adjustments from changes to the future run rate.\n\n## Operating Schedules and Reporting\n\n- Revenue: preserve volume, price, mix and recognition timing. Roll customers through additions/losses; average billable volume needs a timing assumption.\n- Payroll: distinguish headcount, FTE and paid FTE. Use hire/exit dates and supported proration; convert annual pay but do not divide monthly pay by 12 again. Keep commission and employer-cost bases explicit; do not invent load rates or round away fractional FTE.\n- Opex: distinguish units × rate, fixed fees and one-time adjustments. Seats need not equal headcount.\n- Capital/D&A: use cost, residual value, in-service date, useful life and opening assets' remaining depreciation. Preserve partial periods and disposals; reconcile gross assets, accumulated depreciation and net assets. Bridge cash capex to additions and add back noncash D&A where appropriate.\n- Statements: roll retained earnings using source accounting. Keep working capital, principal, interest and equity distinct; tie cash-flow ending cash to balance-sheet cash. Show needed debt/share schedules; never force a tie with unexplained plugs.\n- Variances: compare matching periods and bases; show material monetary variance as amount and percent. Label expense over/under-budget and favorable/unfavorable direction. Missing/zero denominators are unavailable, not 0%. Reconcile driver bridges; align charts and requested commentary to the selected period/case.\n\n## Valuation and Returns\n\nUse the requested method/date; comps or LBO does not imply DCF. Keep metric periods, net debt and share counts consistent. A DCF shows operating drivers, taxes, D&A, capex, working-capital changes, unlevered cash flow, discounting, terminal value and the applicable enterprise-to-equity bridge. State terminal-value method and discount timing; label missing inputs.\n\nIRR/XIRR requires valid cash-flow signs and timing; do not silently substitute another return. Sensitivities must recalculate the affected financial mechanics and match the model at the base combination.\n\n## Finance Presentation\n\nWrite titles, tab names, labels and commentary in plain business language. Do not use `movement`, `backbone`, `pressure point`, `pain point`, `pressure test`, `proof point` or `durable`, including plural and grammatical variants, in authored Finance text. Name the specific result, driver, variance, assumption or risk instead of substituting another vague or dramatic phrase. Preserve and attribute necessary source-defined labels and exact required quotations.\n\nIn working model areas, numeric editable inputs are blue, same-sheet formulas black, cross-sheet links green and external-file links red. On output views such as Summary, Exec Summary, Dashboard or Overview, results use black or dark brand text, including linked numbers. Preserve header contrast, editable-control cues and meaningful warning/status colors. Show the linked selected-case name in green, including on outputs; this exception does not turn output result rows green. Apply these conventions by section when working calculations and outputs share a tab; do not impose Finance formula colors on non-Finance operational trackers.\n\nUse accounting formats: parenthesized negatives, dash zeros, one decimal for percentages, two for per-share prices, and enough precision for fractional FTE/scaled amounts. Currency symbols belong on main/first monetary rows, totals and ending balances across periods, not counts or rates. Keep numeric metric rows numeric: show a runway in months or `n.a.`, with explanations such as cash generation in a separate note. Avoid double-scaling. Indent supporting labels visibly with the text format `  @` (two leading display spaces), not stored spaces. Italicize percentage and ratio rows, including labels and values. Keep totals flush left.\n\nFor financial period headers, use these compact defaults unless user, locale or reference/template conventions specify otherwise. Full dates follow the main skill's locale-appropriate short-date rule.\n\n| Period | Display format | Example |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Week start | `\"Week of \"d-mmm` on the first business day's date | `Week of 13-Jul` |\n| Month | `mmm-yy` on a real date | `Jul-26` |\n| Calendar year | `yyyy` for a stored date; retain a numeric year as a year | `2026` |\n\nUse `Q#:YY` for Finance quarter labels, such as `Q3:26`, and `FY:YY` for fiscal years, such as `FY:26`. Derive both from the stated fiscal calendar and year-label convention. Do not invent either. Excel has no quarter number-format token, so calculate a quarter display label while preserving the underlying date/period. Use `2026` for a regular calendar year, not `FY:26`.\n\nFor new substantial models, use narrow A:B gutters and content from C; optional faint `x` section markers support navigation. Do not impose these gutters on raw data or compact calculators.\n\n## Finance Audit and Verification\n\nReconcile financial schedules and bridges. For nonnegative flows, annual assumptions cannot imply a negative remainder after actuals. Follow [Checks and Audit](../SKILL.md#checks-and-audit). Show differences to two decimals, including `0.00`. Passing differences use neutral text even when cross-sheet formulas would normally be green. Use conditional light-red fill and bold red text above an absolute tolerance appropriate to the unit. Missing or untested checks are unavailable, not zero/PASS. Name failed reconciliations and source cells.\n",
      "source": "../2026-09-15-artifact-tool-reference/files/sources/skill/domain_guidance/financial_models.md",
      "notes": [

      "code": "## Marketing/Advertising Guidance\n\nUse for campaign, funnel, lead, CRM, attribution and advertising-performance tasks. Follow [Domain Requirements](../SKILL.md#domain-requirements) for financial planning or valuation, including work for a marketing company; add the relevant marketing metric definitions without replacing Finance conventions.\n\nIf any specific rule conflicts with user's request or reference, always prioritize the user's request first, then reference/template then general defaults.\nUse [Style guidance](../style_guidelines.md) for shared formatting; the task and intentional reference determine the presentation, not the employer's industry.\n\nFor read-only questions, inspect relevant source records, calculations, definitions, units, periods and protocols without modifying/exporting, changing inputs, adding helper fields/checks or refreshing sources. Report gaps and failed checks rather than repairing them. Authoring defaults apply only to requested creation or edits; preserve original source records and narrow-edit scope.\n\nDistinguish extract freshness from analysis time, and trace requested campaign, channel or funnel outputs to their calculations and sources while preserving the comparison basis.\n\n### Tab structure\n\n- Keep source data, analysis and stakeholder outputs clearly distinguishable without treating those roles as mandatory tabs. Use separate sheets when import/refresh boundaries, calculations, different readers or an explicit request justify them; a compact report may combine compatible roles in labeled regions while preserving the raw data.\n- Clearly name tabs by content (e.g., “Leads_Q1_2025”, “Pipeline Analysis”, “ROI Dashboard”) so that users can easily find inputs versus results.\n\n### Cell formatting\n\n- Use target-based emphasis only when it helps the requested comparison and the source supplies the target and better/worse direction. Make the meaning clear with text or a legend; do not invent targets or require branding, traffic-light colors or KPI cards for every report.\n\n### Marketing Analysis\n\n- Follow [Formula Construction](../SKILL.md#formula-construction) and [Choosing Formulas and Excel Tools](../SKILL.md#choosing-formulas-and-excel-tools) for campaign/channel aggregation. Preserve the metric grain, denominator and comparison basis.\n- Keep time-series dates typed and consistently formatted. Add an ISO export/helper column only when a downstream interface requires it and the requested scope permits it; do not convert the working date axis to text or add unused helpers.\n\n### Raw data vs. outputs\n\n- Keep raw data, including import data, intact and separate from any modifications\n- Perform authorized cleaning, such as excluding test entries or combining categories, in derived columns or a prepared area when needed. Preserve the raw export and record exclusions or mappings. Feed the analysis from that prepared data without adding a tab merely to repeat it.\n- Output figures should follow traceable calculations from the intact sources, whether those roles occupy separate sheets or clear regions on one sheet.\n- Include a chart or compact visual only when it clarifies the requested trend, comparison or funnel. Keep its source ranges traceable; do not create a separate dashboard or hide supporting data merely to satisfy this example.\n\n### Metadata and sources\n\n- Document source platforms, extracts and as-of dates once in the appropriate input/source area or above the relevant input table, following [Citation Requirements](../SKILL.md#citation-requirements). Preserve required row-level provenance and short metric headers. Keep period and unit labels on outputs without repeating source footers there.\n- Label any assumptions clearly\n- Consistency is also key: if “CPC” means cost per click, ensure it’s defined somewhere or obvious from context, so everyone reading the sheet interprets metrics correctly.\n",
      "source": "../2026-09-15-artifact-tool-reference/files/sources/skill/domain_guidance/marketing_advertising.md",
      "notes": [

      "code": "## Healthcare (clinical/administrative) spreadsheets\n\nUse for clinical records, care delivery, patient/encounter analysis and healthcare administration tasks, not every workbook at a healthcare organization. Follow [Domain Requirements](../SKILL.md#domain-requirements): financial forecasts, budgets, cash planning and valuation use Finance guidance, with relevant healthcare definitions, protocols and units added when needed.\n\nIf any specific rule conflicts with user's request or reference, always prioritize the user's request first, then reference/template then general defaults.\nUse [Style guidance](../style_guidelines.md) for shared formatting; apply the healthcare requirements below only where the task needs them.\n\nFor read-only questions, inspect relevant source records, calculations, definitions, units, periods and protocols without modifying/exporting, changing inputs, adding helper fields/checks or refreshing sources. Report gaps and failed checks rather than repairing them. Authoring defaults apply only to requested creation or edits; preserve original source records and narrow-edit scope.\n\n### Tab structure\n\n- Keep raw clinical/administrative records distinct from calculations and reports. These are roles, not a mandatory three-tab template: use separate tabs when different datasets, access, refresh or review needs justify them; otherwise use clearly separated regions without changing original records.\n- In a clinical context, you might have one sheet for patient-level data (each row = one patient or encounter), and another that summarizes by clinic or month.\n- A staff list and appointment schedule may need separate tabs when their records or update owners differ.\n- Name each tab descriptively, such as “Appointments_RawData”, “Clinic KPI Dashboard”.\n\n### Formatting\n\n- Highlight fields staff actually need to complete, following the reference's input styling. Record-only fields may be useful without feeding formulas, but their purpose must be clear; do not add unused input-looking placeholders.\n- When the requested workflow needs clinical or follow-up flags, use only source/protocol-defined thresholds and preserve their severity meanings. Use bounded conditional formatting and include a legend when its meaning is not already clear.\n- Use clear data formatting (e.g. YYYY-MM-DD or MM/DD/YYYY as required), identifiers (like medical record numbers), and units for all measurements (e.g. weight in kg, temperature in °C).\n- For intended printed or urgent use, keep identifiers and relevant clinical information scannable without crowding. Follow [Freeze panes](../style_guidelines.md#freeze-panes) for long lists.\n\n### Formulas\n\n- For clinical indicators such as average length of stay or readmission rates, preserve the source definitions, periods and denominators. Use [Choosing Formulas and Excel Tools](../SKILL.md#choosing-formulas-and-excel-tools) for aggregation.\n- Where calculations involve thresholds or guidelines (say, flagging patients with BMI over a certain value), consider referencing those thresholds from a single cell named “BMI_threshold” so that it’s clear and adjustable, rather than embedding the number in multiple formulas.\n- Follow [Checks and Audit](../SKILL.md#checks-and-audit) for relevant completeness and reconciliation checks. Independently verify critical clinical calculations against an authoritative source or qualified review and state when that verification is unavailable. Use only source-supported thresholds and definitions; do not invent clinical advice or change source protocols.\n\n### Raw data and outputs\n\n- Never alter or delete original healthcare data\n- For data entries that need correction (e.g., a misspelled diagnosis or an out-of-range age), consider doing it via a data validation process or noting corrections in a separate column (“Corrected value”) rather than overwriting, or maintain an audit log of changes.\n\n### Metadata, units, and codes\n\n- Healthcare data is full of codes and units, which must be documented.\n- Always provide the units for each metric (e.g., blood glucose “mg/dL”, heart rate “bpm”).\n- Include normal or target ranges only when the clinical task needs them and an applicable source/protocol supplies the range and context; do not infer a universal range.\n- Keep code definitions available in a labeled region or a separate Codebook sheet when its size, reuse or review purpose warrants it; preserve existing definitions and source codes.\n- If the main data uses abbreviations (like “M”/“F” for sex or clinic codes like “NYC” for New York Clinic), ensure there is a legend or the full term in the header (“Sex (M/F)” is clear).\n",
      "source": "../2026-09-15-artifact-tool-reference/files/sources/skill/domain_guidance/healthcare.md",
      "notes": [

      },
      "code": "## Scientific Research Guidance\n\nUse for research observations, experiments, lab measurements, surveys, statistical analysis and reproducibility tasks. Follow [Domain Requirements](../SKILL.md#domain-requirements) for other functions: a research organization's financial forecast uses Finance guidance, not research-data formatting solely because of its industry.\n\nIf any specific rule conflicts with user's request or reference, always prioritize the user's request first, then reference/template then general defaults.\nUse [Style guidance](../style_guidelines.md) for shared formatting; apply the data-table requirements below to the relevant research records and interfaces.\n\nFor read-only questions, inspect relevant source records, calculations, definitions, units, periods and protocols without modifying/exporting, changing inputs, adding helper fields/checks or refreshing sources. Report gaps and failed checks rather than repairing them. Authoring defaults apply only to requested creation or edits; preserve original source records and narrow-edit scope.\n\n### Tab structure & naming\n\n- Keep raw observations intact in a clearly identified flat table, with one variable per column and one observation per row. Raw, processed and results are distinct roles, not a mandatory number of worksheets.\n- Put cleaning or transformations in separate columns/regions or a processed-data sheet when needed; never overwrite original measurements. Choose separate sheets for substantive transformations, refresh boundaries, reproducibility or review needs, and preserve the requested source layout.\n- Document cleaning steps and protocol in an existing appropriate region or a dedicated sheet when their extent warrants it. Add Calculations or Results sheets only for a distinct analytical or reader purpose, not to expand a simple raw-data export.\n\n### Formatting\n\nFor raw/processed data tables consumed by analytical tools:\n\n- Each column should contain one type of data (with units in the header, not mixed into the cells) and each row one record.\n- Avoid merging cells or creating multi-row headers that can complicate data import into analysis tools.\n- Do not use formatting (color, bold, italics) as the sole means to encode information, since analytical software may not recognize it. When flags are needed, use a labeled value column rather than a cell comment or color alone.\n- Layout should be plain and data-focused: for instance, list any comments or notes in a separate column rather than as Excel cell comments or text boxes. This makes the data more machine-readable.\n\n### Formula practices\n\n- In scientific spreadsheets, complex data analysis is often done outside Excel, but when using formulas, prioritize transparency and accuracy.\n- For requested randomization or simulation, document the method and inputs and preserve the protocol's reproducibility requirements. Follow [Choosing Formulas and Excel Tools](../SKILL.md#choosing-formulas-and-excel-tools) for formula choices.\n- Avoid unrequested circular references. If a required protocol or reference uses iteration, follow [Circular References and Iterative Calculation](../SKILL.md#circular-references-and-iterative-calculation) and document its reproducibility implications.\n- Show meaningful calculation steps under [Build Structure and Formula Flow](../SKILL.md#build-structure-and-formula-flow), without adding helpers for trivial expressions. Cross-check consequential calculations where possible and report limitations. Preserve the recorded protocol, source units and original measurements; distinguish flags, missing observations, simulation/randomness and assumptions without silently changing the analysis design.\n",
      "source": "../2026-09-15-artifact-tool-reference/files/sources/skill/domain_guidance/scientific_research.md",
      "notes": [
        "The concise working pattern is a reading aid. The complete archived document is available under Code and saved record.",

      "code": "## Handling queries and questions\nThe user may ask questions about the sheet instead of requesting an edit or a change. \n- Answer spreadsheet questions from available context without unintended edits. Use the selected workflow's read tools for relevant values, formulas, tables and objects.\n- For a read-only question, do not modify or export the workbook. Report issues instead of repairing them.\n- Locate the requested output by its row and column labels and period, inspect its displayed value and formula, and trace formula precedents to labeled assumptions or raw inputs instead of stopping at an intermediate total.\n- Calculate, reconcile and cite sources from underlying values/formulas.       "code": "## Importing or extracting data from screenshots or reference images\n- When a reference image or screenshot is provided, use appropriate data formats (e.g. number/date formats) based on the workbook topic, audience and purpose instead of trying to recreate the rendered format with just text. Preserve numeric/date usability even when the screenshot shows locale-specific punctuation or currency symbols.\n- Use formulas when appropriate and correct: For screenshot recreation, do not bulk-write numeric tables as all static values until you have separated any clearly formula-derived ranges; test adjacent numeric rows/columns for exact repeated relationships such as sums, differences, products, ratios, or constant multiples, then keep inputs hardcoded and write derived ranges as formulas.\n- Match visible styling, but do not infer intentional formatting from ambiguous image artifacts such as zoom, antialiasing, or compression. Infer font weight only from relative contrast or clear semantics; if all visible text has the same apparent weight, use normal weight.\n",

      "code": "# Artifact Template Selection\n\nOpen the template selection picker for creating new spreadsheets when the user has not provided a template, reference, or visual direction. Also open the picker when the user asks to browse or upload templates. Do not open it if the user declines templates, requests a connected-source design search, or if `list_artifact_templates` is unavailable this turn. Subject matter, audience, tone, company names, and source files do not by themselves specify a template or visual direction.\n\nCall `list_artifact_templates({artifactKind, request})` with `artifactKind: \"spreadsheet\"`, or `\"google-sheets\"` for Google Sheets requests. Include compatible Office and Google templates without changing the requested output format.\n\nRank templates by relevance, breaking ties in favor of personal or shared templates. Include a mix of styles. Pass their `skillName` values unchanged to `choose_artifact_template({artifactKind, request, templates})` and call it once. Set `includeAllTemplates: true` only when the user requests the full catalog. The picker displays at most ten templates.\n\nFollow the selected template or uploaded reference. Save an uploaded reference only when `saveForFutureUse` is true. Use Template Creator with the returned `displayName`. Continue without a template if the picker is declined, cancelled, unavailable, or fails. Do not replace the picker with `request_user_input` or a chat list. Browsing templates does not authorize artifact creation.\n",

      "code": "## Google Sheets-targeted output\n### New Creations\n\nFor a net-new Google Sheets request, create and verify a local `.xlsx` with this skill first. The native Google Sheets deliverable must then be produced by the Google Drive plugin's spreadsheet import action, `mcp__codex_apps__google_drive_import_spreadsheet`, with `upload_mode: \"native_google_sheets\"`.\n\nDo not use Computer Use, Browser Use, blank-Google-Sheets creation plus Google Sheets write APIs, or another direct-to-Sheets construction path for net-new Google Sheets unless the user explicitly asks for that alternate workflow. If they do, mention first that output quality is expected to be best when a local `.xlsx` is imported through the Google Drive plugin.\n\nIf the Google Drive plugin is unavailable, use the plugin-install/user-elicitation flow to ask the user to install `google-drive@openai-curated`. If the plugin is available but `_import_spreadsheet` is missing, ask the user to reinstall or refresh the Google Drive plugin before continuing with the native Google Sheets deliverable.\n\nAfter successful native import, the user-facing deliverable is the Google Sheets link. Treat the local `.xlsx` as a build artifact unless the user explicitly asks to keep or receive it.\n\n### Edits\n\nUse the Google Drive plugin's Google Sheets skill for edits to existing Google Sheets. The local `.xlsx` creation and native import workflow above applies only to net-new Google Sheets deliverables.\n",

w=Workbook.create(),s=w.worksheets.add('Model');\ns.getRange('A1:C3').values=[['Quantity','Price','Revenue'],[2,10,null],[3,10,null]];\ns.getRange('C2').formulas=[['=A2*B2']];s.getRange('C2:C3').fillDown();\nconst before=structuredClone(w.toProto()),input=s.getRange('B2:B3').values,captures=[];\ntry{for(const price of [8,10,12]){s.getRange('B2:B3').values=[[price]];w.recalculate();const values=s.getRange('C2:C3').values;assert.deepEqual(values,[[2*price],[3*price]]);captures.push({price,values});}}\nfinally{s.getRange('B2:B3').values=input;w.recalculate();}\nassert.deepEqual(s.getRange('C2:C3').values,[[20],[30]]);\nconst length/i.test(v)))findings.push(v);\nassert.deepEqual(findings,[]);\nconst       "code": "import fs from 'node:fs/promises';\nimport path from 'node:path';\nimport {spawn} from 'node:child_process';\nimport {fileURLToPath} from 'node:url';\nimport {Workbook} from '@oai/artifact-tool';\nimport {artifactSession} from '@oai/artifact-tool/artifact-session';\nconst root=path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)),out=path.join(root,'files/runs'),sessionRoot=path.join(root,'files/local-sessions');\nawait fs.mkdir(sessionRoot,{recursive:true});\nconst pkg=path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.resolve('@oai/artifact-tool')));\nconst child=spawn(process.execPath,[path.join(pkg,'artifact-session-mcp/server.mjs')],{stdio:['pipe','pipe','pipe']});\nconst pending=new Map;let id=0,buffer='',stderr='';\nchild.stderr.on('data',d=>{stderr+=d;});\nchild.stdout.on('data',d=>{buffer+=d;let n;while((n=buffer.indexOf('\\n'))>=0){const line=buffer.slice(0,n);buffer=buffer.slice(n+1);try{const r=JSON.parse(line),p=pending.get(r.id);if(p){clearTimeout(p.timer);pending.delete(r.id);p.resolve(r);}}catch{}}});\nfunction rpc(method,params={}){return new Promise((resolve,reject)=>{const current=++id;const timer=setTimeout(()=>{pending.delete(current);reject(new Error('MCP response timed out'));},30000);pending.set(current,{resolve,reject,timer});child.stdin.write(JSON.stringify({jsonrpc:'2.0',id:current,method,params})+'\\n');});}\nconst results=[];\nasync function call(label,args,meta){const response=await rpc('tools/call',{name:'artifact_session_run',arguments:args,...meta?{_meta:meta}:{}});results.push({label,input:args,response});await fs.writeFile(path.join(out,'sessions.json'),JSON.stringify(results,null,2));console.log(label,JSON.stringify(response.result?.structuredContent??response.error));return response;}\ntry{\n results.push({label:'initialize',response:await rpc('initialize',{protocolVersion:'2025-11-25',capabilities:{},clientInfo:{name:'artifact-reference-probe',version:'1'}})});\n const schema=await     {
      "id": "support-isolation",
      "title": "Isolate risky examples in workers",
      "kind": "script",
      "category": "Study harness",
      "status": "Executed",
      "summary": "Give each API example its own process, fixture, timeout and saved receipt so one failure does not erase the rest.",
      "input": {
        "script": "api-sweep.mjs",
        "role": "Research harness around the package",
        "runtime": "Bundled Node; local dependencies prepared first"
      },
      "result": {
        "receipt": "files/runs/api-example-results.json",
        "interpretation": "The complete captured output is linked below."
      },
      "code": "import fs from 'node:fs/promises';\nimport path from 'node:path';\nimport {spawn} from 'node:child_process';\nimport {fileURLToPath} from 'node:url';\nconst root=path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)),out=path.join(root,'files/runs');\nconst entries=(await fs.readFile(path.join(out,'api-help.ndjson'),'utf8')).trim().split('\\n').map(JSON.parse).filter(x=>x.kind==='api').flatMap(x=>(x.examples||[]).map(example=>({name:x.name,...example})));\nconst selected=process.env.API_INDICES?new Set(process.env.API_INDICES.split(',').map(Number)):null;\nconst jobs=entries.map((entry,index)=>({entry,index})).filter(x=>!selected||selected.has(x.index)),results=[];\nasync function worker(){for(;;){const job=jobs.shift();if(!job)return;const start=Date.now();const result=await new Promise(resolve=>{const c=spawn(process.execPath,[path.join(root,'explore.mjs'),'api-worker',String(job.index)],{stdio:['ignore','ignore','pipe']});let stderr='',timedOut=false;c.stderr.on('data',chunk=>{if(stderr.length<1500)stderr+=chunk.toString().slice(0,1500-stderr.length);});const t=setTimeout(()=>{timedOut=true;c.kill('SIGKILL');},15000);c.on('close',(code,signal)=>{clearTimeout(t);resolve({code,signal,timedOut,stderr});});});results.push({name:job.entry.name,index:job.index,ms:Date.now()-start,...result});await fs.writeFile(path.join(out,'api-sweep.json'),JSON.stringify(results,null,2));if(results.length%25===0)console.log(results.length,'/',entries.length);}}\nawait Promise.all(Array.from({length:4},()=>worker()));const all=[];for(let i=0;i<entries.length;i++){try{all.push(JSON.parse(await fs.readFile(path.join(out,'api-example-'+String(i).padStart(3,'0')+'.json'),'utf8')));}catch{all.push({index:i,...entries[i],worker:results.find(x=>x.index===i)});}}\nawait fs.writeFile(path.join(out,'api-example-results.json'),JSON.stringify(all,null,2));console.log('Completed',all.length,'API examples.');\n",
